tips.scene: One beat of your video — a few seconds with its own image, video, and narration.
tips.still: The picture this scene starts from. Get this right before rendering video — stills are fast, video is slow.
tips.clip: The few seconds of video for this scene, animated from its still image.
tips.narration: What the voice says during this scene. Its length sets how long the scene runs.
tips.storyboard: All your still images in order — the plan for the video before any video is rendered.
tips.seed: Same prompt and seed give the same result. Change it for a different take.
tips.model: Use a different AI model for just this shot. Leave on Auto to use your default.
tips.motion: How the camera moves — plain words work: 'slow push in', 'orbit right', 'handheld', 'static'.
tips.length: How much source video to render. The narration still decides how long the scene plays.
tips.trim: Cut seconds off the start or end of this clip.
tips.overlay: Text drawn on screen during this scene.
tips.pin: Locks this exactly as it is. Regenerating and prompt edits skip it until you unpin.
tips.createFinal: Re-renders any draft scenes at full quality, then builds your MP4. Drafts are for deciding — do this when you're happy.
tips.duck: Automatically turns the music down whenever the narrator is speaking.
tips.beat: Nudges scene changes to land on the music's beat.
tips.captionsBurn: Captions are drawn onto the video itself. Always visible, works everywhere.
tips.captionsSidecar: Captions come as a subtitle file (.srt) viewers can turn on or off.
tips.proEditor: Sends your scenes, audio and timeline to a pro editor for manual finishing.
tips.voice: Which narrator speaks — a style like "deep male" or a Kokoro id. Empty uses the default.
tips.speed: 1.0 is normal. The scene re-times to match the new length.
tips.ownImage: The clip animates from your picture instead of the generated still.
tips.transition: How one scene flows into the next.
tips.resume: Queue whatever this project still owes. Useful if the engine stopped mid-render and the board is waiting on work that is no longer in the queue.
tips.publishKit: Writes a title, description and hashtags from your script, and renders a thumbnail to go with them. Nothing is uploaded anywhere.
tips.applyEdit: Make the changes listed above. Until you press this, nothing has been touched.
tips.audioLane: The sound under your cut: one row for the narration in each scene, one for the music. A gap means nothing has rendered there yet.
tips.rewriteScript: Ask for a new screenplay from your note. The storyboard is rebuilt from it, so scene-level edits are replaced.

glossary.def: One beat of your video — a few seconds with its own image, video, and narration.
The picture this scene starts from. Get this right before rendering video — stills are fast, video is slow.
The few seconds of video for this scene, animated from its still image.
What the voice says during this scene. Its length sets how long the scene runs.
All your still images in order — the plan for the video before any video is rendered.
A fast preview render. It's re-rendered at full quality when you create the final video.
Rendered at full quality. This is what goes in your video.
Being generated right now. You can keep working — nothing here blocks you.
Waiting its turn. Your computer renders one thing at a time.
Same prompt and seed give the same result. Change it for a different take.
Locks this exactly as it is. Regenerating and prompt edits skip it until you unpin.
How one scene flows into the next — cut, crossfade, or dip to black.
On the video: drawn in, always visible. Separate file: a subtitle file viewers can turn off.
Re-renders any draft scenes at full quality, then builds your MP4. Drafts are for deciding — do this when you're happy.
Sends your scenes, audio and timeline to a pro editor for manual finishing.
LocalCut AI's grade for this machine's hardware, S (best) to C, from GPU memory, RAM and disk. The tier decides which models are recommended — a lower tier gets lighter picks, not fewer features.

A model served outside the engine — for example a script model running in Ollama, or narration and captions running as companion processes. Nothing to download in LocalCut AI; the stage still runs fully on this machine.
A saved project shape — its scenes, models and settings, with no generated media. Start a new video from one on Home.
Everything this machine has made: videos and one-off tool outputs, filtered and searched in one place.
A recorded identity a regenerate displaced — its seed, model and params. Selecting one back is a swap, not a re-render, while its file survives.
Where a music bed's end meets its start when it loops in a video. The preview plays that joint back to back.
Your image as a clip's source: the video animates from it instead of a generated keyframe.
Audio uploaded with the consent affirmation, for cloning a speaker. Without the affirmation, audio arrives as a plain asset that cloning refuses.
One step of the render in the flowchart — a still, a clip, the narration, the final cut. What feeds it are its inputs.
Everything that feeds a node plus everything it feeds. Select a node in the flowchart and its chain lights up while the rest dims, so you can see what a change will touch.

A suggested thumbnail plus a title, description and hashtags, written from your script. Built on request once the video is finished - it renders like anything else, so it takes a moment and can be regenerated.
What an instruction WOULD change, worked out and shown before anything happens. Nothing is saved, queued or recorded until you press Apply.
The graphics card could not fit a render. The engine retries it smaller on its own; when even that fails it says so and offers the ways out - a smaller size, a lighter model, or cloud hardware.
A zip holding this app's logs, its versions and the system report — what a bug report needs, in one file. Nothing is sent anywhere; you choose where to save it. Settings → About.
Third-party ComfyUI nodes: Python that runs unsandboxed with access to your models, files and network. Enabling one in Settings → Workflows records that you allow code you already installed yourself.
A ComfyUI graph exported with Save (API Format), imported so a custom model can render through it. Checked against the node packs you have enabled before it is stored.
A %%TOKEN%% placeholder in a workflow, filled per render. A workflow with none still renders — it just renders the same thing every time.
